info.name: Prafi API
info.description:
Backend API (Express + Sequelize + PostgreSQL).

**Setup (once)**
1. Import this collection and `Prafi-Local.postman_environment.json`.
2. Select **Prafi Local** in the environment dropdown (top right).
3. In **Prafi Local**, set `superadminPassword` (same as SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env) in the **Current value** column, then Ctrl+S.

**Automatic saving**: after every Login, the token is saved to the environment as `{{token}}` (last logged-in user) and `{{superadminToken}}` / `{{adminToken}}` / `{{tenantToken}}`. Register and Upload save `adminEmail`, `tenantEmail`, `imageId`, `imageUrl`. Each save is printed in the Postman Console. Scripts write the environment **Current value** (Initial value stays empty on purpose).

**Collection Runner**: turn on *Keep variable values* (Persist responses / variables) so values from the run stay in the environment afterwards.

**Roles**: superadmin → can create admin, admin → can create tenant.

**Responses**: `{ success: true, data }` or `{ success: false, error: { code, message, details? } }`. Error `message` and `details[].message` are in Bahasa Indonesia (ready to show in the frontend); `code` and `field` stay in English, so frontend logic should switch on `code`, not on the message text.

**Activation**: new **admin** accounts start inactive and must be activated by a superadmin before they can log in (the collection does this right after Register - Admin). New **tenant** accounts sign up publicly (no token) and are active right away.

**Token**: every request uses `{{token}}` (collection → Authorization), which each Login request sets to the account that just logged in. Log in as the role a request needs first — the request names say which, e.g. "(by Superadmin)", "(tenant)", "(admin)". The role tokens (`superadminToken`, `adminToken`, `tenantToken`) are still saved, but no request uses them.

**Tokens**: role-specific requests use their own token (`{{superadminToken}}`, `{{adminToken}}`, `{{tenantToken}}`). Requests without their own auth (Me, Update Me, List Users) use the collection default `{{token}}` = whoever logged in last.

**Tenants**: tenant users manage their own tenant profile at `/api/tenants/me`; superadmin/admin read all at `/api/tenants`.

**Tenant categories**: superadmin/admin manage them at `/api/tenant-categories`; every tenant profile needs a `categoryId`.

**Notifications**: every role gets notifications at `/api/notifications` (see folder 9 for the list of types and who receives them).

`POST /api/auth/register/tenant` — **public sign-up, no token needed**: anyone can create a tenant account. The tenant is **active right away** (`approval.isActive = true`) and can log in immediately.

Body: `firstName`, `lastName`, `phoneNumber`, `email`, `password` (min 8), `tenantName` — all required; `faceImageId` optional (from **Upload Image**). No `role` needed (the URL decides it).

request.description: Logs in as the tenant created above. The token is saved to `{{tenantToken}}`. Also saved to `{{token}}` (the last logged-in user).
Any logged-in user. Returns the profile including `faceImage` (with its full `url`).

Any logged-in user updates **their own** account . There is no id in the URL, so nobody can update another user.

Send only the fields to change:
- `firstName`, `lastName`, `phoneNumber`, `email` (non-empty strings; email must be unique)
- `faceImageId`: id from **Upload Image**, or `null` to remove it (each image belongs to one user)
- `password` (min 8) **together with** `currentPassword`

Not allowed (400): `id`, `role`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, unknown fields, empty body.

Errors: 400 validation / wrong currentPassword, 401 no token, 409 email or faceImageId used by another user.

**Changing your password here does not update `{{newUserPassword}}`**, so the Login requests for this user will fail until you change it back or update that variable.

item.name: 7. Tenant Categories
item.description:
Tenant categories (`/api/tenant-categories`). Only **superadmin** and **admin** can create, read, update and delete tenant categories; tenants get 403. All requests use the Bearer `{{token}}`.

Every tenant profile needs a `categoryId`, so this folder creates one and saves it to `{{categoryId}}` for **8. Tenants**. It also shows update, a 404-free read, and deleting an unused category. A category that tenants still use cannot be deleted (409 `STILL_IN_USE`).

item.name: 8. Tenants
item.description:
Tenant profile endpoints. **Rules:** a **tenant** user creates, reads, updates and deletes **only their own** tenant profile at `/api/tenants/me` (one profile per tenant user). **superadmin / admin** read every tenant (`GET /api/tenants`, `GET /api/tenants/:id`) but cannot create/update/delete. All endpoints use the Bearer `{{token}}`.

Runs in order: tenant uploads a logo → creates its profile → reads/updates it → admin lists all tenants → superadmin reads one by id → tenant deletes it.

**Needs `{{categoryId}}`:** it is set by **7. Tenant Categories → Create Tenant Category**. If it is missing, Create My Tenant stops with a clear error.

item.name: 9. Notifications
item.description:
Notifications for every role (`/api/notifications`, Bearer `{{token}}`). They are created automatically by the actions earlier in the collection.

| type | who gets it | when |
|---|---|---|
| `ADMIN_PENDING_ACTIVATION` | superadmin | a new admin is registered (needs activation) |
| `PRODUCT_SUBMITTED` | superadmin, admin | a tenant creates a product |
| `USER_DEACTIVATED` | superadmin | an admin deactivates a user account |
| `PRODUCT_DEACTIVATED` | superadmin | an admin deactivates a product |
| `PRODUCT_PUBLISHED` | admin | an admin activates a product (now on the landing page) |
| `PRODUCT_UPDATED` | admin | a tenant updates a product |
| `TENANT_PROFILE_UPDATED` | admin | a tenant updates their tenant profile |
| `TENANT_REGISTERED` | admin | a new tenant signs up |
| `PRODUCT_UNDER_REVIEW` | tenant (owner) | they create a product |
| `PRODUCT_APPROVED` | tenant (owner) | their product is activated |

Each notification: `id`, `type` (switch on it in the frontend), `name` (title), `description` (message), `entityType` + `entityId` (what to open: `user`, `product` or `tenant`), `isRead`, `readAt`, `createdAt`. Every user only ever sees their own notifications (others → 404).

Endpoints: `GET /api/notifications?page=&limit=&unread=true` (newest first, `meta.unreadCount` for the badge), `GET /api/notifications/unread-count`, `PATCH /api/notifications/:id/read`, `PATCH /api/notifications/read-all`, `DELETE /api/notifications/:id`.

request.description: Logs in as the tenant so the next requests (which all use `{{token}}`) run as that user.

`GET /api/notifications` — your own notifications, newest first. Query: `page`, `limit` (max 100), `unread=true` for unread only. `meta.unreadCount` = badge number. Saves the newest id to `{{notificationId}}`.

item.name: 11. Cleanup & Logout
item.description: Deletes the uploaded image, then logs out every role (tenant, admin, superadmin) and checks each logged-out token is rejected. Run this folder last: after it, every saved token is revoked, so run the Login requests again before other requests.

request.description: Requires **tenant** role (current rule in `image.routes.ts`). Deletes the DB row and the file. Users using this image get `faceImageId = null`.

Any role (superadmin, admin, tenant). Revokes the token sent with this request: it is rejected from now on, even before it expires. Only this token is logged out, the user's other sessions (other devices/logins) keep working. Logging out the same token twice returns 401. After logging out, run the matching Login request to get a new token.
The tenant's logged-out token now gets 401 "Token has been revoked".
